title: The red-green cycle, with both runs recorded
instruction: In the sandbox model, run one complete red-green cycle and keep BOTH runs. (1) Write a small class ConDemoDiscount with a static rateForTier(int) that is deliberately unfinished — it returns 0 for every tier. (2) Scaffold its test with generate_object(mode="pattern", pattern="systest", attributes=["SysTestGranularity(SysTestGranularity::Unit)", "SysTestCheckInTest"]) and replace the scaffold body with ONE real assertion: tier 2 must be 10 percent. (3) Build and run with run_systest_class. The build must be CLEAN and the test must FAIL — red means a failing assertion, never a broken file, and the failure message must name the expected and actual values. (4) Now fix rateForTier and change NOTHING about the test. Build and run again; it must pass. The pair is the evidence: a green document alone cannot tell a working test from an empty one, which is why this case commits the red run beside the green one. Note that the runner says nothing on a red run carrying a real assertion message — that is deliberate, because the same note would fire on a genuine regression.
